name: 43797-sharedprefixdecode-gptoss120b-4gpu
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3, four GPUs of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:4), NVLink between the cards and PCIe to a host with 208 CPUs and 1.86 TB of DRAM.
parallelism: TP=4, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine. No router, no remote store, no NIC on the serving path.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=24, bounded at 96 requests with a 330 s safety cap, warmup the first 48 requests by completion. Static seed 43797, so both runs draw the same prefix sequence.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, SINGLE TURN. 8 distinct shared prefixes of 1024 tokens (`prefix_buckets` with prefix_count 8, bucket_weight 100), one drawn uniformly at random per request, plus 64 unique prompt tokens of its own, generating exactly 3072 tokens, greedy. The checkpoint's chat template prepends a fixed header carrying a `Current date:` line stamped from the clock, so the engine reports roughly 1200-1250 prompt tokens rather than 1088 -- that is the template, not drift.
purpose: A long-form writing assistant on four GPUs serving 24 concurrent users from eight shared system prompts, generating 3072 tokens each.
launch:
# The engine's command line. `kv-offloading-size` is GiB summed across all TP ranks.
#
# The host tier is sized against the workload in `scenario.json`, not picked round. This
# checkpoint costs 36 layers x 2 (K,V) x 8 KV heads x 64 x 2 B = 73728 B of KV per token summed
# across the 4 ranks, and `CPUOffloadingSpec` sizes its host pages from exactly that quantity, so
# 1 GiB of tier is 1073741824 / 73728 = 14563 tokens. The workload's 8 shared heads occupy
# 8 x 1024 = 8192 of those, i.e. 56% of the tier, which leaves the rest for the per-request tails.
model: openai/gpt-oss-120b
dtype: bfloat16
tensor-parallel-size: 4
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.92
max-model-len: 10240
enable-prefix-caching: false
kv-offloading-size: 1
kv-offloading-backend: native

# Do not add `block-size`: this checkpoint is HYBRID (18 sliding-window layers at window 128, 18
# full-attention), so the engine resolves mutually divisible per-group block sizes itself and
# pinning one number can make that resolution fail or silently repartition the KV cache.
